title: Variable IO flagged minimums with grace period probe
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: Customers building streaming-heavy features (real-time chat, live captioning, incremental code suggestions) have variable input/output ratios and often spike initial calls during warmup. Existing per-token minimums penalize bursty warmups and discourage smaller customers from trying streaming features. Goal: test a hybrid minimum that flags streaming sessions and applies a short grace period (first N seconds or first M tokens) during which IO consumption is not billed against the usual per-minute minimum. After the grace period the call transitions to standard billing with a variable IO floor that scales with observed input-heavy or output-heavy patterns. Hypothesis: a short grace period reduces signup friction for streaming features, improves trial conversion for teams under 100k monthly tokens, and increases adoption of streaming without materially reducing unit revenue for enterprise customers. Success metrics: 1) Trial conversion rate for new streaming users (+% absolute), 2) Net revenue per new streaming account over 90 days (no more than 10% downside vs control), 3) Percent of streams that remain below grace thresholds (indicates low abuse), 4) Customer support incidents related to billing questions. Measurement plan: randomized A/B for new streaming-enabled API keys over 6 weeks, cohorts split by estimated monthly usage and region. Instrumentation needed: flags on streaming session start, token counters separated by input/output, billing event logs annotated with grace start/end, dashboard showing distribution of session lengths and IO ratios. Rollout: start with a lightweight probe for non-enterprise accounts and self-serve signups; if safe, expand to all self-serve. For enterprise customers require opt-in gating (contract addendum) and add telemetry to avoid contract arbitrage. Billing implications: requires changes to metering layer to mark grace-period tokens and to not count them toward minimums for the defined window; reconciliation job to handle late-closed streams. Contract/security: recommend a short addendum clause for enterprise contracts clarifying grace-period behavior and abuse protections (rate limits, automated anomaly detection). Operational guardrails: hard limits on grace duration per-account, automatic throttling if abuse patterns detected, and a rollback safety net to revert billing rules for a subset of customers. Edge cases: partially-closed streams, long-lived idle websockets, and cross-region fallbacks. Risks/mitigations: revenue leakage if grace thresholds too generous (mitigate with small initial N and conservative M), increased complexity in billing reconciliation (eng backlog & automated tests), and customer confusion (amp up console messaging and invoicing line items). Next steps: finalize instrumentation spec with ENG, draft contract addendum with Legal, prepare quickstart docs and console UX copy with DX, and schedule the A/B run.
